11.01.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what do you ask the parents?"
- "The parents' complaint: limp, deformity, in-toeing, bow legs, flat feet."
- "Then birth, milestones and family; each points to a group of diseases."

### The parents' complaint
| Complaint | Think of |
|---|---|
| Painless limp, short leg from walking age | late DDH |
| Painful limp, 4–8 years | Perthes disease |
| Limp or out-toeing, teenager | SUFE |
| Limp with fever | septic hip or bone — urgent |
| In-toeing, both sides | femoral anteversion, tibial torsion, metatarsus adductus |
| Bow legs or knock knees | physiological, rickets, Blount disease |
| Toe walking, tires easily (boy) | Duchenne; tone up → diplegia |
| Flat feet | flexible, familial; painful teenager → coalition |

- DDH = developmental dysplasia of the hip; SUFE = slipped upper femoral epiphysis
- Tibial torsion and anteversion remodel by 7–9 years in 95% (Exam Techniques)
- One-sided or fast deformity → look for a real cause

[[FIG: Fig 11.1 — In-toeing: patellae point inwards · 11.01

### Birth, milestones, family
| Ask | Why |
|---|---|
| First born, breech, tight womb | DDH risk |
| Swaddling with legs tied straight | turns an unstable hip into a dislocation |
| Prematurity, neonatal jaundice, meningitis | cerebral palsy (CP) |
| Difficult labour, big baby | obstetric brachial plexus palsy (→ ch 6) |
| Milestones late | CP, myopathy, syndrome |
| Family with the same problem | dysplasia, rickets, neuropathy, DDH |
| Sun exposure, diet | nutritional rickets |

- First born is the strongest DDH risk
- **Memory:** **BMF** — birth, milestones, family

#### Milestones (Exam Techniques)
| Age | Can do |
|---|---|
| 3 months | lifts head prone |
| 9–12 months | pulls to stand |
| 15 months | walks alone |
| 2 years | runs |
| 3 years | jumps |
| 5 and 6 years | hops, then skips |

- **Memory:** head 3, stand 9, walk 15; run 2, jump 3, hop 5, skip 6

#### Ask every time
| Complaint | Ask |
|---|---|
| Deformity | when noticed? better or worse? one side or both? |
| Limp | painful? since walking? fever? |
| Treatment | casts, braces, operations, drugs |
| Function | walks, runs, stairs, school |

- **Red flags:** night pain, fever, rapid progression, one-sided change → infection or tumour
- General interview → ch 1

11.02.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "examine this child"
- "Play and watch; general look; walk; stand: alignment and deformity."
- "Supine: lengths, hips, rotation; prone: the rotational profile."
- "Then feel, move, special tests, neuro; spine and the other side."

- **Whole paediatric exam (video):** [▶ The Physio Channel (pGALS) · 2:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p85eVqFC5C8)

### The route on one page
| Position | What you do (in order) |
|---|---|
| Watch and play | how the child moves, sits, stands up |
| General | face, stature, skin, spine markers, laxity |
| Walking | gait, foot progression angle, patellae |
| Standing | patellae forward · knee gaps, blocks · Trendelenburg, Adam's |
| Sitting | transmalleolar axis; knee flexion test |
| Supine | lengths, Galeazzi, abduction, Thomas, DDH tests by age |
| Prone | hip rotation, Craig, thigh-foot angle, heel bisector, Ely, Staheli |
| Finish | feel, move, Silfverskiöld, neuro, spine, upper limbs |

- **Memory:** **5 points of Look** — gait, rotational profile with length, deformity, scars, general disease (Kasr Al-Ainy)

### Watch, play, general look
- Watch from the door, while the parents talk
- Toddlers on the parent's lap
- Undress in stages; talk to the child, not only the parents

| Look at | Clue |
|---|---|
| Sclerae | blue → osteogenesis imperfecta |
| Height, parents' height | short stature → dysplasia or rickets |
| Skin | café-au-lait spots → neurofibromatosis |
| Lower back | dimple, hair tuft, lipoma → spinal dysraphism |
| Body sides | one side bigger → hemihypertrophy |
| Joints | hyperlaxity → Beighton score (→ ch 1) |

- **Memory:** **FASHS** — face, stature, skin, spine, sides

### Walking
- Walk away and back; again from the side
- Watch arms too: posturing → hemiplegia
- Name the gait; then the foot progression angle (11.3)

| Gait | Think of |
|---|---|
| Short-limb, toe-walking | unilateral DDH, LLD |
| Waddling, deep lordosis | bilateral DDH, coxa vara |
| Toe walking | habit, Duchenne, diplegia |
| Scissoring, crouch, jump | CP (11.4) |
| High-stepping | foot drop: neuropathy, spina bifida |
| Calcaneus ("peg") | weak calf: polio, clubfoot overcorrected |

- LLD = limb length discrepancy
- Waddling toddler → think bilateral DDH, not "calcium deficiency" (Prof Abdel-Ghani)

### Standing
#### Look and measure
- Patella facing **forward** before judging any knee deformity (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Varus: medial malleoli touching → intercondylar distance
- Valgus: knees touching → intermalleolar distance

| Then | Why |
|---|---|
| Pelvis tilted → blocks under the short leg | LLD |
| Trendelenburg, each leg | abductors, DDH |

[[FIG: Fig 11.2 — Varus measured, patellae forward · 11.02

#### Feet and spine
- Forward bend (Adam's) for scoliosis → ch 9
- Plumbline from the occiput should pass through the natal cleft

### Supine
- Stand on the child's **right** side; never examine from the left (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Squaring, true and apparent length → ch 7
- Galeazzi, abduction in flexion, Thomas (11.4)

| Age | Hip tests |
|---|---|
| Under 3 months | Ortolani, Barlow |
| Before walking | limited abduction, Galeazzi, asymmetric folds |
| Walking | short leg, Trendelenburg, waddling, telescoping |

- **Memory:** clunk → abduction → limp (newborn, crawler, walker)

[[FIG: Fig 11.3 — Supine for lengths and rotation · 11.02

### Prone, then finish
| Step | Do |
|---|---|
| Prone | rotational profile from the foot up (11.3) |
| Feel | pulses, tenderness, warmth, swelling |
| Move | active before passive — the difference matters |
| Finish | neuro, spine, upper limbs; "I would examine the other side" |

PITFALL — "the sitting child looks like a flexion deformity"
- Sitting gives an apparent fixed flexion deformity (FFD); supine shows none (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Say → "**Supine the knee extends fully: no fixed flexion deformity.**"

11.03.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "this child in-toes: where from?"
- "Foot progression angle tells in or out; then femur, tibia or foot."
- "Femur: prone hip rotation and Craig. Tibia: thigh-foot angle, transmalleolar axis. Foot: heel bisector."

- **Memory:** Staheli profile = **F-H-T-T-H** — foot progression, hip rotation, thigh-foot, transmalleolar, heel bisector
- Order on the couch: distal to proximal — foot, tibia, femur

### The five measurements
| Measure | How | Normal (Miller) |
|---|---|---|
| Foot progression angle | foot axis vs walking line | −5° to +20° |
| Hip internal rotation | prone, knee 90° | 20–60° |
| Hip external rotation | prone, knee 90° | 30–60° |
| Thigh-foot angle | prone, knee 90°; thigh vs foot axis | 0–20° external |
| Transmalleolar axis | sitting; malleoli vs knee axis | about 20° external (Exam Techniques) |
| Heel bisector | prone; line through the heel | 2nd–3rd toe web (Kasr Al-Ainy) |

- Prone internal rotation over 70° → femoral anteversion
- Thigh-foot angle under −10° → internal tibial torsion
- Heel bisector toward the 3rd–5th toes → metatarsus adductus

[[FIG: Fig 11.4 — Staheli profile · 11.03

| Source | In-toeing | Out-toeing |
|---|---|---|
| Femur | anteversion | retroversion |
| Tibia | internal torsion | external torsion |
| Foot | adduction | abduction (flat foot) |

- **Memory:** same word, same direction — "in" in every segment gives in-toeing

[[FIG: Fig 11.5 — Anteversion → toe-in; retroversion → toe-out · 11.03

### Femur
- Prone, pelvis held still, knee 90°; leg falls out = internal rotation
- "W" sitting → anteversion; Craig (Gage) test → ch 7
- Anteversion: 40° at birth, 20° at 9 years, 15° at maturity (Exam Techniques)

[[FIG: Fig 11.6 — Infant hip rotation · 11.03
[[FIG: Fig 11.7 — Craig test · 11.03

### Tibia
- Thigh-foot angle: hold the **leg**, not the foot — the foot has play (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- Foot deformed (clubfoot) → use the transmalleolar axis
- Course case: thigh-foot angle 45° external → external tibial torsion

[[FIG: Fig 11.8 — Thigh-foot angle, prone · 11.03
[[FIG: Fig 11.9 — Transmalleolar axis · 11.03

### Patella while walking
| Patella | Foot | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Forward | in or out | below the knee: tibia or foot |
| In or out | in or out | femur |
| In (squinting) | forward | anteversion plus external tibial torsion |

[[FIG: Fig 11.10 — Squinting patellae · 11.03

### Genu varum and genu valgum
| | Genu varum | Genu valgum |
|---|---|---|
| Stance | ankles touch, knees apart | knees touch, ankles apart |
| Measure | intercondylar distance | intermalleolar distance |

- Normal: both gaps zero; record in cm or finger-breadths
- Record before treatment; review every 2–3 months when young

[[FIG: Fig 11.11 — Knee gaps measured · 11.03

#### Physiological curve (Exam Techniques)
| Age | Knee |
|---|---|
| Birth | 10–15° varus |
| 18 months | straight |
| 3 years | 10–15° valgus |
| 7 years on | about 7° valgus (adult ≈6°, → ch 8) |

- **Memory:** bow at birth, straight at 1½, knock at 3, settle by 7
- Wait for varum until 4–5 years; valgum until 6–7 years (Prof Abdel-Ghani)

[[FIG: Fig 11.12 — Knee angle by age · 11.03

#### When is it pathological?
- Beyond the age limits, worsening, one side, or a short child
- Lateral thrust in stance, internal tibial torsion → Blount
- Rickets: whole-limb bowing; Blount: proximal tibia only

#### Femur or tibia? The knee flexion test
| Deformity with knees flexed 90° | Source |
|---|---|
| Disappears | femur |
| Less but some left | femur and tibia |
| Unchanged | tibia |

- **Memory:** flexion abolishes the femoral part (Kasr Al-Ainy; Nagah)

- Say → "**Patellae forward, soft tissue noted; I would confirm on a standing film.**"

11.04.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "the tests that change with age"
- "Newborn: Ortolani and Barlow. Crawler: abduction and Galeazzi. Walker: limp and Trendelenburg."
- "CP: Thomas, Staheli, Ely, Phelps, popliteal angle, Silfverskiöld — one tight muscle each."

### Is the infant hip dislocated?
#### Ortolani test
- **Aim:** reduce a dislocated newborn hip
- **How:** baby supine, hip and knee 90°; fingers on the trochanter; abduct and lift
- **Positive:** clunk as the head slips in → dislocated but reducible hip
- **Why:** abduction plus lift brings the head over the rim
- **Trap:** a click means nothing; useful under 3 months (Nagah)
- **Video:** [▶ JAMA Network · 1:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYezLZ5qRSs)

[[FIG: Fig 11.14 — Barlow, then Ortolani · 11.04

#### Barlow test
- **Aim:** find a dislocatable (unstable) newborn hip
- **How:** same grip; adduct and push the thigh backwards
- **Positive:** clunk as the head slips out → dislocatable hip
- **Why:** provocative test of a lax capsule
- **Trap:** do it once, gently; repeating harms the hip
- **Video:** [▶ American Family Physician · 2:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fBq9LaCEOic)

| | Barlow | Ortolani |
|---|---|---|
| Starts | located | dislocated |
| You | push out | bring in |
| Positive means | dislocatable | dislocated, reducible |

- **Memory:** **B**arlow = **B**ack out; **O**rtolani = **O**n (in)
- Ortolani negative in a dislocated hip → irreducible, rigid type

[[FIG: Fig 11.15 — Ortolani clunk; less abduction · 11.04

### Is the crawling or walking hip dislocated?
#### Limited abduction in flexion
- **Aim:** late sign of DDH after 3 months
- **How:** child supine, hips and knees flexed 90°; abduct both together
- **Positive:** less abduction on one side → that hip dislocated
- **Why:** the adductors shorten once the head rides up
- **Trap:** bilateral DDH limits both equally
- **Video:** [▶ Children's Hospital Colorado · 4:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=69kWyAsSMRE)

[[FIG: Fig 11.16 — Full and limited abduction · 11.04

#### Galeazzi test (child)
- **Aim:** femoral shortening of a dislocated hip
- **Positive:** knee behind (side view) → short femur = dislocated hip; reading → ch 7
- **Trap:** equal knees in bilateral DDH; technique → ch 7
- **Video:** [▶ Ibrahim Salem · 1:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C37Yvrgy19A)

[[FIG: Fig 11.17 — Unequal knee heights · 11.04

#### Klisic test
- **Aim:** high-riding trochanter of a dislocated hip (Nagah)
- **How:** supine; line from the GT tip through the ASIS, both sides
- **Positive:** lines meet off the midline → one hip; below the umbilicus → both
- **Why:** the trochanter rides up with the dislocated head
- **Trap:** same idea as Schoemaker's line (→ ch 7); works in bilateral DDH
- **Video:** [▶ IHDI Online (infant hip exam) · 2:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4-9FsXgDRDI)

[[FIG: Fig 11.34 — Klisic (Schoemaker) lines: GT to ASIS, normally crossing at the umbilicus · 11.04

| Other DDH signs | Point |
|---|---|
| Asymmetric folds | thigh or labial, before walking |
| Telescoping | piston movement of the femur → ch 7 |
| Trendelenburg | walking child; level the pelvis first |
| Lump sign | femoral head felt in the groin |

[[FIG: Fig 11.18 — Telescoping infant hip · 11.04

- Trendelenburg → ch 7 (7.4); unreliable under 4 years (McRae)

### How bad is the clubfoot?
#### Pirani score
- **Aim:** severity and follow-up of clubfoot
- **How:** six signs, each 0, 0.5 or 1; score in the corrected position
- **Positive:** 6 = worst; over 4 → tenotomy usually needed (Dr Fathey)
- **Why:** the score guides casting and tenotomy
- **Video:** [▶ OrthopaedicsPG · 4:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Z-zbwtYl74)

| Midfoot | Hindfoot |
|---|---|
| Lateral border curve | Posterior crease |
| Medial crease | Empty heel |
| Talar head uncovered | Equinus |

- **Memory:** three in the middle, three at the back — curve, crease, head; crease, heel, equinus

[[FIG: Fig 11.19 — Pirani signs · 11.04

#### Clubfoot flexibility (correctability)
- **Aim:** is the deformity correctable?
- **How:** thumb on the talar head, abduct the foot round it; then dorsiflex
- **Positive:** fully, partly or not correctable → flexible, partly, rigid
- **Why:** rigid feet suggest syndromic or neglected clubfoot
- **Trap:** feel the talar head, not the calcaneus (Dr Fathey)
- **Video:** [▶ Global HELP · 2:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Y_qGYYlW7c)

[[FIG: Fig 11.20 — Thumb on the talar head · 11.04

- Look: **CAVE** — cavus, adductus, varus, equinus; deep creases
- Dorsalis pedis absent in about 20% (Nagah)
- Always look at the spine and hips

[[FIG: Fig 11.21 — CAVE deformity · 11.04

### Will the in-toeing foot correct itself?
#### Forefoot adduction correction test
- **Aim:** metatarsus adductus: flexible or rigid
- **How:** hold the heel; abduct the forefoot
- **Positive:** past neutral → corrects itself; to neutral or less → casts (Hoppenfeld)
- **Why:** a flexible foot remodels with growth
- **Video:** [▶ MedOne · 1:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3C5Ibkc0XQg)

[[FIG: Fig 11.22 — Forefoot abducted past neutral, or not · 11.04

### Is this flat foot flexible?
- Tiptoe or Jack test → ch 10 (10.3): arch forms, heel to varus = flexible
- Rigid → coalition, vertical talus, arthrogryposis
- Flexible flat foot with a tight heel cord needs treatment

### Which muscle is tight in CP?
- **Memory:** one test per tight muscle — Thomas or Staheli (psoas), Ely (rectus), Phelps (gracilis), popliteal angle (hamstrings), Silfverskiöld (calf)
- Barlow and Ortolani have no place in CP; check abduction and telescoping
- Phelps → ch 7 (7.4); Silfverskiöld → ch 10 (10.3)

#### Thomas test in CP
- **Aim:** hip flexion contracture (iliopsoas)
- **How:** child holds the other knee to the chest; you flatten the lordosis
- **Positive:** thigh rises → FFD = the angle; full technique → ch 7
- **Video:** [▶ Ibrahim Salem · 4:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T2z48jOecnA)

[[FIG: Fig 11.23 — Thomas test in a child · 11.04

#### Staheli prone extension test
- **Aim:** hip FFD in CP, more accurate than Thomas
- **How:** child prone, legs over the couch end; extend one hip
- **Positive:** buttock starts to rise → thigh angle = FFD
- **Why:** both hips flexed flatten the lordosis
- **Video:** [▶ Saikat · 1:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m9T0TFC00AY)

#### Duncan-Ely test
- **Aim:** tight or spastic rectus femoris
- **How:** child prone; you flex the knee quickly
- **Positive:** buttock rises → tight rectus femoris (stiff-knee gait)
- **Why:** rectus crosses hip and knee → ch 7
- **Video:** [▶ UniSC Sport and Fitness · 0:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KKyaZgSRSr8)

#### Popliteal angle
- **Aim:** hamstring tightness or spasticity
- **How:** child supine, hip 90°; extend the knee; sound side first
- **Positive:** angle short of extension over 20° → tight hamstrings (Exam Techniques)
- **Why:** hip flexion pre-stretches the hamstrings
- **Trap:** read at the first resistance; forcing lifts the leg (Kasr Al-Ainy)
- **Video:** [▶ Ibrahim Salem · 2:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=duPkmPLb7aw)

11.04.1.b:
#### Ortolani test
- **Aim:** reduce a dislocated newborn hip
- **How:** baby supine, hip and knee 90°; fingers on the trochanter; abduct and lift
- **Positive:** clunk as the head slips in → dislocated but reducible hip
- **Why:** abduction plus lift brings the head over the rim
- **Trap:** a click means nothing; useful under 3 months (Nagah)
- **Video:** [▶ JAMA Network · 1:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYezLZ5qRSs)

[[FIG: Fig 11.14 — Barlow, then Ortolani · 11.04

#### Barlow test
- **Aim:** find a dislocatable (unstable) newborn hip
- **How:** same grip; adduct and push the thigh backwards
- **Positive:** clunk as the head slips out → dislocatable hip
- **Why:** provocative test of a lax capsule
- **Trap:** do it once, gently; repeating harms the hip
- **Video:** [▶ American Family Physician · 2:53](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fBq9LaCEOic)

| | Barlow | Ortolani |
|---|---|---|
| Starts | located | dislocated |
| You | push out | bring in |
| Positive means | dislocatable | dislocated, reducible |

- **Memory:** **B**arlow = **B**ack out; **O**rtolani = **O**n (in)
- Ortolani negative in a dislocated hip → irreducible, rigid type

#### Limited abduction in flexion
- **Aim:** late sign of DDH after 3 months
- **How:** child supine, hips and knees flexed 90°; abduct both together
- **Positive:** less abduction on one side → that hip dislocated
- **Why:** the adductors shorten once the head rides up
- **Trap:** bilateral DDH limits both equally

- **Positive:** knee behind (side view) → short femur = dislocated hip; reading → ch 7

#### Klisic test
- **Aim:** high-riding trochanter of a dislocated hip (Nagah)

#### Pirani score
- **Aim:** severity and follow-up of clubfoot
- **How:** six signs, each 0, 0.5 or 1; score in the corrected position

|---|---|

| Talar head uncovered | Equinus |

11.05.b:
MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "two-minute paediatric short case"
- "Spot: age, gait, deformity, scars. Do: the one or two tests that prove it."
- "Say: one diagnosis and one differential."

### DDH in the walking child
- **Spot:** limp, short leg, toe-walking on that side; waddling if both
- **Do:** limited abduction, Galeazzi, telescoping, Trendelenburg
- **Say:** "Left DDH, late presentation. Differential: septic hip sequel."

[[FIG: Fig 11.27 — Short leg from DDH · 11.05

### Clubfoot — treated or neglected
- **Spot:** small foot, thin calf, scars; neglected → rigid deformity
- **Do:** CAVE, Pirani, correctability; spine, hips and pulses
- **Say:** "Right idiopathic clubfoot, partially correctable. Differential: syndromic clubfoot."

[[FIG: Fig 11.28 — Bilateral clubfoot · 11.05

### Cerebral palsy — diplegia or hemiplegia
- **Spot:** diplegia: both legs, scissor or crouch; hemiplegia: arm and leg one side
- **Do:** Thomas, popliteal angle, Silfverskiöld, hip abduction; GMFCS level
- **Say:** "Spastic diplegia, GMFCS II, tight calves. Differential: idiopathic toe walking."

- Diplegia: legs worse than arms, often premature, usually walk by about 4 years
- Hemiplegia: arm worse than leg; may have a short limb

### Genu varum — physiological, rickets or Blount
- **Spot:** bowed legs, ankles touching; short, broad wrists → rickets
- **Do:** intercondylar distance; knee flexion test; lateral thrust on walking
- **Say:** "Bilateral genu varum, likely rachitic. Differential: Blount disease."

| | Physiological | Rickets | Blount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Age | under 3–4 years | any growing child | obese walker |
| Shape | symmetric, mild | whole limb | proximal tibia, asymmetric |
| Clue | improving | rosary, broad wrists, short | lateral thrust |

### Genu valgum
- **Spot:** knees touch, ankles apart; older than 7 years is a concern
- **Do:** intermalleolar distance with patellae forward; knee flexion test
- **Say:** "Bilateral genu valgum, likely rickets. Differential: skeletal dysplasia."

[[FIG: Fig 11.29 — Dysplastic genu valgum · 11.05

### Perthes disease or SUFE
- **Spot:** Perthes: 4–8 years, limp; SUFE: teenager, out-toeing
- **Do:** Perthes: early loss of abduction in flexion, then internal rotation
- **Do:** SUFE: hip rolls into external rotation as it flexes (Exam Techniques)
- **Say:** "Left SUFE, chronic. Differential: Perthes sequel."

[[FIG: Fig 11.30 — Perthes and SUFE films · 11.05

### Flat foot in a child
- **Spot:** flat arch standing, heel valgus, "too many toes"
- **Do:** tiptoe, Jack, Silfverskiöld → ch 10
- **Say:** "Flexible flat feet with hyperlaxity. Differential: tarsal coalition."

[[FIG: Fig 11.31 — Supple foot arches off load · 11.05

### In-toeing
- **Spot:** patellae in, W-sitting, in-toeing gait
- **Do:** Staheli profile: hip rotation, thigh-foot angle, heel bisector
- **Say:** "Increased femoral anteversion, both sides. Differential: internal tibial torsion."

### Arthrogryposis
- **Spot:** stiff joints, thin limbs; all four limbs in about half
- **Do:** shoulders adducted, elbows extended, wrists flexed; rigid clubfeet
- **Say:** "Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (amyoplasia). Differential: distal arthrogryposis."

[[FIG: Fig 11.32 — Multiple congenital contractures · 11.05

### Spina bifida
- **Spot:** back scar or lipoma, wasted legs, cavovarus feet
- **Do:** level: motor, dermatomes, reflexes; bladder; hips
- **Say:** "Low lumbar myelomeningocele, cavovarus feet. Differential: hereditary sensorimotor neuropathy."

[[FIG: Fig 11.33 — Cavovarus feet, wasted legs · 11.05

- "Child, age, complaint, since when; gait; deformity standing; rotational profile; tests."

| Tests | "Beighton raised; Thomas and Silfverskiöld negative." |

| Metabolic | rickets, renal osteodystrophy |
| Growth plate | Blount, physeal arrest |
| Dysplasia | achondroplasia, pseudoachondroplasia |
| Neuromuscular | CP, spina bifida, polio |

| In-toeing | patellae in | Staheli profile |
| Arthrogryposis | stiff, creaseless joints | rigid clubfeet, elbows extended |
| Spina bifida | back scar, cavovarus | neuro level, bladder |
